learnings: File selection must distinguish AUR-controlled files (PKGBUILD, .install, local patches) from upstream source tree files (src/<pkgname>/...). Files under src/ are extracted from verified tarballs and should be lowest priority unless referenced by PKGBUILD functions.

Models need explicit guidance that 'upstream code doing something questionable' is not an AUR injection. The audit should check: is this file part of the AUR repo, or part of the extracted source? Is it executed during build/install?
Patch files (.patch) should not be auto-classified as binary - they are typically text diffs. The binary detection logic may need adjustment.

When a model flags upstream source code as unsafe, the reasoning should be rejected outright per the threat model boundary: 'What the application does when it runs is the vendor's product, not an injection.'
